anomalies.observed: J4 is labeled “I2C”, but its two signal pins connect to NET0012 and NET0011. NET0011 is also the ATtiny RESET/PB5 net and has a 10 kΩ pull-up to +5V through R6.
anomalies.expected: An I2C connector should expose two usable I2C signal pins. Using the MCU reset pin as one of them requires disabling its reset function, which removes normal reset-based programming and conflicts with the net’s reset pull-up role.

evidence.quote: J4 value “I2C”; pins 1 and 3 are labeled NET0012 and NET0011; U3/U4 pin 1 is labeled “RESET/PB5”; R6 is 10K between +5V and NET0011. Sheet /, page 1.

anomalies.impact: The advertised I2C interface cannot operate as a conventional two-GPIO I2C interface while preserving the MCU’s reset function; firmware and programming may be impaired.

anomalies.observed: The LM1117-5.0 regulator U2 has only a 100 nF capacitor, C1, shown from its +5V output to GND.
anomalies.expected: An LM1117-family regulator generally requires a substantially larger output capacitor, commonly at least 10 µF, for stability; 100 nF alone is inadequate for the usual application.

evidence.quote: U2 value “LM1117-5.0”; C1 value “100nF” connected between +5V and GND. Sheet /, page 1.

anomalies.impact: The regulator may oscillate or respond poorly to load changes, resulting in an unstable +5V rail.

parsed.summary: The drawing labels J4 as an I2C connector but connects one signal to the MCU reset net. It also shows only 100 nF on the LM1117 output, below the usual capacitance required for regulator stability.
